## Perspective Audit Summary

**Component/artifact reviewed:** Mega-Menu Navigation With Hover-Only Submenus
**Perspectives escalated for deep review:** Keyboard & Motor Access (HIGH), Screen Reader & Semantic Structure (MEDIUM), Cognitive & Neurodivergent (MEDIUM)
**Perspectives at LOW (not reviewed):** Magnification & Reflow, Environmental Contrast, Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity, Auditory Access

### Findings by Severity

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| CRITICAL | 2 |
| MAJOR | 1 |
| MINOR | 1 |
| ENHANCEMENT | 0 |

### Perspectives That Passed
None. All escalated perspectives surfaced findings requiring remediation.

### Perspectives With Findings — Grouped by ARRM Role

**Front-End Dev**
- Submenu unreachable for keyboard users — Keyboard & Motor Access — CRITICAL — WCAG 2.1.1
- Submenu content not rendered in DOM for non-mouse users — Screen Reader & Semantic Structure — CRITICAL — WCAG 4.1.2 / 2.1.1
- Focus indicator clipped by negative outline-offset — Keyboard & Motor Access — MINOR — WCAG 2.4.7, 2.4.13

**UX Design**
- Hover-only interaction pattern creates motor/cognitive barrier — Cognitive & Neurodivergent — MAJOR — WCAG 2.5.1 / APG Guidelines

**Visual Design**
- (None)

**Content Author**
- (None)

### Open Questions Requiring Human Verification
None. All findings are code-level and enforceable from source review. No captions, transcripts, alt text quality, or reading level assessments required.

### Recommended Next Step
**BLOCK** — CRITICAL findings present — do not ship until resolved. Keyboard users cannot access submenu content, and screen reader users will never encounter it due to conditional DOM rendering.

---

## Detailed Findings by Escalated Perspective

### 1. Keyboard & Motor Access (HIGH)

**Finding:** Submenu content is conditionally rendered in the DOM only when `openMenu === item.id`, which is exclusively triggered by `onMouseEnter`. Keyboard users cannot open or interact with the submenu, completely blocking navigation to child pages.
**WCAG:** 2.1.1 Keyboard
**Perspective:** Keyboard & Motor Access
**Severity:** CRITICAL
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (primary) / UX Design (secondary)
**Evidence:** `onMouseEnter={() => setOpenMenu(item.id)}` and conditional JSX `{item.children.length > 0 && openMenu === item.id && (<div className="submenu"> ... })}`
**Fix:** Replace mouse-driven state with a keyboard-focus or click-toggle pattern. Ensure submenu links are always present in the DOM (visually hidden until toggled) or implement `role="menubar"` / `role="menuitem"` patterns with proper `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` attributes.

**Finding:** Focus indicator on `.submenu-link` uses `outline-offset: -2px`, which clips the focus ring inside the padding area, reducing its visible contrast change against adjacent colors and violating focus visibility requirements.
**WCAG:** 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.4.13 Focus Not Obscured
**Perspective:** Keyboard & Motor Access
**Severity:** MINOR
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (primary) / Visual Design (secondary)
**Evidence:** CSS `.submenu-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #005fcc; outline-offset: -2px; background: #e3f2fd; }`
**Fix:** Remove `outline-offset: -2px` or use a positive offset so the focus ring sits outside the padding. Ensure the combined outline + background shift maintains ≥3:1 contrast change against adjacent colors.

### 2. Screen Reader & Semantic Structure (MEDIUM)

**Finding:** Submenu links are conditionally rendered based on mouse hover state. Screen reader and voice control users will never see or navigate to submenu content because it is absent from the DOM until `onMouseEnter` fires. This breaks programmatic name, role, and value association for assistive technologies.
**WCAG:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value / 2.1.1 Keyboard
**Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure
**Severity:** CRITICAL
**Route to:** Front-End Dev (primary) / UX Design (secondary)
**Evidence:** JSX conditional rendering `{openMenu === item.id && (<div className="submenu"> ... })}` prevents DOM injection for non-pointer users.
**Fix:** Render submenu links unconditionally in the markup but hide them visually with CSS (`opacity: 0; visibility: hidden;` or `clip-path`) until toggled. Use `aria-expanded` on the parent trigger and `aria-controls` linking to the submenu container so screen readers can announce state changes and navigate content reliably.

### 3. Cognitive & Neurodivergent (MEDIUM)

**Finding:** Hover-only menu interaction requires precise pointer control and causes unexpected content appearance. This pattern is explicitly discouraged in WAI-APG for users with motor impairments, tremors, or cognitive processing differences, as it creates unpredictable layout shifts and demands sustained hover precision without a reliable abort mechanism.
**WCAG:** 2.5.1 Pointer Cancellation / APG Menus Pattern Guidelines
**Perspective:** Cognitive & Neurodivergent
**Severity:** MAJOR
**Route to:** UX Design (primary) / Front-End Dev (secondary)
**Evidence:** `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` handling without keyboard or click alternative; CSS `@keyframes slideDown` triggers on hover.
**Fix:** Replace hover-trigger with a click/toggle button or focus-trigger pattern. Provide a clear, persistent visual indicator of the open state (e.g., background highlight, border change) so users can track which menu is active without relying on transient hover states. Ensure `prefers-reduced-motion` suppresses the slide animation to prevent cognitive overload.

---
*Audit completed. All findings are code-level enforceable. No content-level verification required.*
